entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Judoc II of Rožmberk (also known as Jošt II of Rožmberk), who died on December 21, 1467, was a prominent Bohemian nobleman and ecclesiastic whose career significantly intertwined with the political and religious turmoil of 15th-century Central Europe. A member of the powerful Rožmberk family, one of the wealthiest and most influential noble houses in the Kingdom of Bohemia, Judoc navigated the complex landscape of the Hussite Wars and the subsequent regency periods. His dual roles as a secular lord and a high-ranking church official made him a pivotal figure in both Bohemian internal affairs and the broader European religious sphere, particularly within the Holy Roman Empire.

His ecclesiastical career saw him rise to the influential position of Bishop of Wrocław, a diocese critical for its strategic location and economic importance within Silesia. Beyond his episcopal duties, Judoc also served as the Grand Prior of the Order of St. John (Knights Hospitaller) for Austria and Bohemia. This dual appointment granted him considerable temporal and spiritual authority, allowing him to wield influence over significant landholdings and military resources. He participated in various diets and negotiations, striving to maintain the Rožmberk family's power amidst the protracted succession crises following the death of Emperor Sigismund and the minority of King Ladislaus Posthumus.

entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Judoc II of Rožmberk (Jošt z Rožmberka, 1430–1467) stood as a prominent Bohemian nobleman, ecclesiastical prelate, and military-religious leader during the turbulent mid-15th century. Born into the immensely powerful Rožmberk family, the wealthiest and most influential noble house in the Kingdom of Bohemia, he leveraged his lineage to attain significant positions: Bishop of Wrocław (Breslau) from 1456 until his death, and Grand Prior of the Order of St. John (Knights Hospitaller) for Austria and Bohemia from 1458. His career unfolded amidst the lingering religious schisms of the Hussite era, the rise of the Utraquist King George of Poděbrady, and the continuous geopolitical struggles for dominance in Silesia and Central Europe.

His tenure as Bishop of Wrocław was marked by efforts to stabilize the diocese following decades of Hussite conflict, asserting Catholic authority in a region often caught between Bohemian, Polish, and Imperial interests. Simultaneously, as Grand Prior of the Knights Hospitaller, Judoc was responsible for managing the Order's extensive landholdings and military capabilities across a crucial strategic area, including maintaining fortifications and raising troops. He engaged in complex political maneuvers, often aligning with the Catholic opposition to George of Poděbrady, participating in the 'Green Mountain League' (Zelenohorská jednota) in 1465, which sought to depose the Utraquist monarch. This opposition, rooted in both religious conviction and aristocratic ambition, frequently brought him into direct confrontation with the Bohemian crown.
